correctness.rationale: With a=p/2>2, Q=|1+e^{it}+rho e^{i phi}e^{iNt}|^2, differentiation twice in phi is valid at zeros. The cosine-power Fourier integral gives c=Gamma(p)/(Gamma(a+N)Gamma(a-N+1))<0 because a-N+1 is in (-1,0). Subtracting the rho-linear term from M_phi_phi, using |Q-A|<=5rho and |u|,|u_phi|<=2 bounds the remainder by 36a(a-1)9^(a-2)rho^2. Symmetry makes M_phi zero at phi=0 and pi; integrate error from nearest endpoint and sin phi>=2 min(phi,pi-phi)/pi to get strict derivative and matching 1±rho/r cosine-gap bounds for rho<r. Exact slope and high-k asymptotic follow by squeezing and the gamma-ratio law.
risk: The explicit r is only a sufficient (very small) neighborhood; no global-in-rho monotonicity claim.
The high-degree asymptotic is strictly for infinitesimal rho, not uniformly positive rho.
